question: Under which schedule of the Constitution of India comes the names of states and their territorial jurisdiction? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Fourth
Ninth
Fifth
First
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is First

Explanation:
The First Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains the names of states and union territories along with their territorial jurisdiction. It describes the boundaries and areas of the states. Other schedules deal with different subjects: the Second Schedule deals with salaries and allowances, the Third Schedule with oaths, the Fourth Schedule with allocation of Rajya Sabha seats, the Fifth Schedule with administration of Scheduled Tribes areas, and the Ninth Schedule with land reforms. The First Schedule is crucial for understanding the federal structure of the Constitution.

☛ Second Schedule relates to → Salaries, allowances, and pensions
☛ Fourth Schedule relates to → Allocation of seats in Rajya Sabha

question: Which of the following is not a Union Territory? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Chandigarh
Puducherry
Dadra and Nagar Haveli
Tripura
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Tripura

Explanation:
India has a total of 8 Union Territories. They are Chandigarh, Puducherry, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, and Delhi (National Capital Territory). Tripura is a state, not a Union Territory. India has 28 states. Tripura is a state in northeastern India with its capital at Agartala. It became a full state in 1972. Hence, Tripura is not a Union Territory.

question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन केंद्र शासित प्रदेश नहीं है? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/01/2019) Shift 1)
options_hi: चंडीगढ़
पुदुचेरी
दादरा और नगर हवेली
त्रिपुरा

question: Who was the President of the Order of Business Committee of the Constituent Assembly? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel
Dr. Rajendra Prasad
KM Munshi
Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is KM Munshi

Explanation:
The Constituent Assembly formed various committees to conduct its business smoothly. Among them, the Order of Business Committee was responsible for determining the agenda and order of proceedings of the Assembly. The President (Chairman) of this committee was KM Munshi, a prominent Assembly member and jurist. His full name was Kanhaiyalal Maniklal Munshi. He hailed from Gujarat and made significant contributions to the framing of the Indian Constitution. Other leaders had different roles: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was the Chairman of the Advisory Committee, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Constituent Assembly, and Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru was the Chairman of the Union Powers Committee. Thus, KM Munshi is the correct answer for the Order of Business Committee.

question_hi: संविधान सभा की ऑर्डर ऑफ बिजनेस कमेटी के अध्यक्ष कौन थे? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/01/2019) Shift 1)

question: Who gives India's oath of office to President ? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Union Home Minister
Prime Minister
Chief Justice of India
Parliament
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chief Justice of India

Explanation:
The oath of office to the President of India is administered by the Chief Justice of India. This provision is mentioned in Article 60 of the Constitution. During the oath, the President pledges to uphold the Constitution, protect the nation, and perform duties impartially. In the absence of the Chief Justice, the senior-most Supreme Court judge can administer the oath. The President's term is 5 years, and they are eligible for re-election. The swearing-in ceremony takes place at Rashtrapati Bhavan.

question_hi: भारत के राष्ट्रपति को पद की शपथ कौन दिलाता है? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/01/2019) Shift 2)

भारत के राष्ट्रपति को पद की शपथ भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश दिलाते हैं। यह प्रावधान अनुच्छेद 60 में दिया गया है। शपथ के समय राष्ट्रपति भारत के संविधान का पालन करने, देश की रक्षा करने और न्यायपूर्ण तरीके से कार्य करने का वचन देते हैं। यदि मुख्य न्यायाधीश अनुपस्थित होते हैं, तो वरिष्ठतम सुप्रीम कोर्ट न्यायाधीश शपथ दिला सकता है। राष्ट्रपति का कार्यकाल 5 वर्ष का होता है और वे पुनः चुने जा सकते हैं। शपथ ग्रहण समारोह राष्ट्रपति भवन में आयोजित किया जाता है।

question: Which emergency is called a constitutional emergency? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: National Emergency
State Emergency
Financial Emergency
None of these
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is State Emergency

Explanation:
The Indian Constitution provides for three types of emergencies. Among them, State Emergency (Article 356) is called a constitutional emergency because it is imposed when the constitutional machinery fails in a state. National Emergency (Article 352) is imposed due to war, external aggression, or armed rebellion. Financial Emergency (Article 360) is imposed during financial instability. State Emergency is also known as President's Rule. Under this, the state government is dismissed, and the administration comes under the control of the President. This emergency relates to the federal structure of the Constitution.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Article 352 → National Emergency
☛ Article 356 → State Emergency
☛ Article 360 → Financial Emergency
☛ Another name for State Emergency → President's Rule
☛ Grounds for National Emergency → War, external aggression, armed rebellion
question_hi: किस आपातकाल को संवैधानिक आपातकाल कहा जाता है? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/01/2019) Shift 2)
options_hi: राष्ट्रीय आपातकाल
राज्य आपातकाल
वित्तीय आपातकाल
इनमें से कोई नहीं

भारतीय संविधान में तीन प्रकार की आपातकालीन स्थितियों का प्रावधान है। इनमें से राज्य आपातकाल (अनुच्छेद 356) को संवैधानिक आपातकाल कहा जाता है, क्योंकि यह तब लगाया जाता है जब किसी राज्य में संवैधानिक तंत्र विफल हो जाता है। राष्ट्रीय आपातकाल (अनुच्छेद 352) युद्ध, बाहरी आक्रमण या सशस्त्र विद्रोह के कारण लगाया जाता है। वित्तीय आपातकाल (अनुच्छेद 360) वित्तीय अस्थिरता के समय लागू होता है। राज्य आपातकाल को राष्ट्रपति शासन के नाम से भी जाना जाता है। इसके तहत राज्य सरकार बर्खास्त कर दी जाती है और राज्य का प्रशासन राष्ट्रपति के नियंत्रण में आ जाता है। यह आपातकाल संविधान के संघीय ढांचे से संबंधित है।

question: On the basis of anti-defection law, who decides disqualification in the case of Rajya Sabha? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Leader of the Opposition
President
Speaker
Chairman
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chairman

Explanation:
Under the anti-defection law (10th Schedule), the disqualification of Rajya Sabha members is decided by the Chairman of Rajya Sabha (the Vice-President of India). This law was added by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment (1985). The Chairman's decision in this matter is final and cannot be challenged in court (similar to Article 122). For Lok Sabha, the decision is made by the Speaker.

☛ Which schedule contains the anti-defection law? → 10th Schedule
☛ Who decides disqualification in Lok Sabha? → Speaker
☛ Who appoints the Chairman of Rajya Sabha? → Vice-President is ex-officio Chairman
☛ How many members are required to avoid defection? → At least 2/3 of the original party

question: An ordinance issued by the President of India is made under? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/01/2019) Shift 2)

President's Judicial Power
solution:

Explanation:
An ordinance issued by the President of India is an exercise of the legislative power of the President under Article 123. question: On whose recommendation can the President of India postpone Article 370? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Governor
Council of Ministers
State legislative assembly
Parliament
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is State legislative assembly

Explanation:
Under Article 370 of the Indian Constitution, the President has the power to modify or postpone the special provisions for the state of Jammu and Kashmir. However, this power can only be exercised on the recommendation of the state's Constituent Assembly or State Legislative Assembly. According to Article 370(1)(d), the President can issue orders only with the concurrence of the state's Constituent Assembly. After the dissolution of the Constituent Assembly, this power was transferred to the State Legislative Assembly. Therefore, the President of India can postpone Article 370 only on the recommendation of the State Legislative Assembly. This provision was created to grant special status to Jammu and Kashmir, but it was abrogated on 5 August 2019.

question: The suspension of fundamental rights has been taken from which Constitution? (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: British Constitution
Germany's Weimar Constitution
Japanese Constitution
French Constitution
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Germany's Weimar Constitution

Explanation:
The concept of suspension of fundamental rights in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from Germany's Weimar Constitution of 1919. The Weimar Constitution had provisions to suspend certain fundamental rights during emergency. Under Article 359 of the Indian Constitution, the President can suspend the enforcement of fundamental rights (except those under Articles 20 and 21) during a national emergency (Article 352). This borrowing reflects the influence of the Weimar Constitution on India's emergency provisions. The Constitution of India adopted several features from the Weimar Constitution, including the suspension of rights during emergencies.

question: Under which Article does the President have the authority to seek consultation from the Supreme Court? (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 1)

Article 143
Article 129

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 143

Explanation:
Article 143 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to seek the opinion of the Supreme Court on any question of law or fact that is of public importance. This consultation is advisory in nature and is not binding on the President. The article has two clauses: the first deals with questions of law, and the second deals with questions that arose before the commencement of the Constitution. This provision ensures coordination between the executive and judiciary. question: The power to make the President's Ordinance is _________. (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Need a Parliamentary Consent
Judicial review is not applicable
Subject to judicial review
Discretionary
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Subject to judicial review

Explanation:
Under Article 123 of the Indian Constitution, the President has the power to promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session. This power is executive in nature, not legislative. However, every ordinance must be laid before both Houses of Parliament and ceases to operate six weeks after reassembly unless approved. The President's ordinance-making power is subject to judicial review. Courts can examine whether the conditions for issuing the ordinance existed and whether it violates fundamental rights or the basic structure of the Constitution. In the landmark case of R.C. Cooper vs. Union of India (1970), the Supreme Court held that ordinances are subject to constitutional limitations and can be challenged in court. Thus, the power is not absolute or discretionary; it can be judicially scrutinized.
